Panther tracks

Each animal has its own colour. Solid-dash = adult, fine-dash = kitten. Enlarged dot = first fix, red = most recent.

FWC aerial telemetry, Jan 2024 – Feb 2026. Fixes average 4 days apart, taken at morning rest sites — lines show sequence, not the route walked. Pick one animal to isolate its track.

Big Cypress ORV: secondary trails are closed under a court settlement; only primary trails are open, and the data doesn't distinguish them. Confirm at a kiosk or the Oasis ORV Office.
Florida: 1,138 segments from FDEP Office of Greenways & Trails (Feb 2026) plus NPS for Big Cypress. FDEP notes their layer is incomplete.
Motorized, yearlong
Motorized, seasonal
Montana: 238 segments, 479 miles, from the Forest Service Motor Vehicle Use Map — Bitterroot and Salmon-Challis. 160 are seasonal; the remaining routes are labeled yearlong in the source. Only motorized routes are included; walk-in trails are not. "Open" means legally open, not passable.

U.S. Forest Service National Forest System Roads for Montana Units 270 and 321. Data service. Reference snapshot, September 2026; not a live closure or passability feed. Verify current access with the managing forest.

Oak habitat

Oak-dominated
Oaks present
SFWMD-verified stand
73,300 acres in Collier & Lee, of which 35,400 on public land.

Oak-dominated covers hammocks, scrub and scrubby flatwoods — live oak, laurel oak, sand live oak, myrtle oak. Inferred from FNAI community type, not surveyed trees; acorn crops swing hard year to year.

Dashed outlines are stands SFWMD photo-interpreters independently called oak — 9,000 acres, of which 2,300 fall outside the inferred layer entirely. Florida only.
